name: Search Funds and Entrepreneurship Through Acquisition
summary: Traditional (funded) search funds, self-funded searches, and the ETA buyer as CEO: the investor underwrites a first-time CEO and a small owner-run company at once. The return engine has mostly been multiple expansion (about 80% of exit value from 6.3x to 15.6x), not operating improvement, so the spine is: rebuild EBITDA from tax returns and bank deposits with the seller's labor at market salary; price at exit multiple equal to entry; fixed-charge coverage in a 20% revenue decline; customer concentration and seller-personal relationships with customer calls before close; seller-note subordination and transition; tranche-vested searcher equity; an experienced board with CEO-replacement rights; and no-poach review for franchise targets. Two eras of data disagree; the 2026 Stanford/IESE studies govern. Named search-fund failure case files were not sourced (GAP).
one_check: Rebuild EBITDA from tax returns and bank deposits with the seller's labor replaced at market salary, then price the deal at an exit multiple equal to entry; if it works only with a re-rating, it is a bet on the exit market, not on the CEO.

subtypes.name: Traditional (funded) search fund
subtypes.description: Investors fund search capital (salary and deal costs) for a right to invest in the acquisition, often with a step-up.

subtypes.name: Self-funded search / ETA acquisition
subtypes.description: Searcher funds the search and raises acquisition equity for an identified target.

intake_questions.question: Are we funding search capital in a traditional search fund, or investing in an acquisition by a self-funded searcher?
How many LOIs has the searcher signed, and how many months into the search?
Is the target a franchise, multi-unit or staffing business?
intake_questions.why: Triggers FDD Item 17 and no-poach review.

intake_questions.question: Is the acquisition financed with an SBA 7(a) loan, senior loan and/or seller note?
intake_questions.why: Triggers leverage, guarantee and subordination items.

intake_questions.question: Has the searcher ever run a P&L?
Will the seller stay for a transition period?

requests.request: Searcher's PPM and search-fund LPA, investor list and step-up terms on search capital.
requests.why: Defines investors' right (not obligation) to invest in the acquisition and the step-up on search capital.
requests.pass: Investor right to invest in the acquisition is a right, not an obligation; step-up stated.
requests.fail: Obligation to fund, or step-up undefined.
requests.verify: Counsel review; confirm investor list with two investors.

requests.request: Searcher equity grant and vesting schedule, split into acquisition, time and performance tranches.
requests.why: Full vesting at close removes the incentive to perform.
requests.pass: Equity earned in tranches for acquisition, time and performance.
requests.fail: Searcher's equity vests fully at close.

requests.request: Searcher's operating history: statement of any P&L ever run, with scope, size and dates.
requests.format: CV and written statement; references named.
requests.why: Most searchers have never run a P&L; first-time CEOs get overwhelmed.
requests.pass: Operating experience documented, or an operating board and coach compensate.
requests.fail: No P&L experience and no operating board.

requests.request: LOI history: every LOI signed, date, target, and why each died.
requests.format: Schedule with dates from search launch.
requests.why: Successful searchers signed 4.6 LOIs on average (first by month six); unsuccessful 8.2; deals died on adverse diligence (59%), valuation (41%), seller retraction (32%), investor support (31%).
requests.pass: First LOI by about month six; reasons for failed LOIs credible.
requests.fail: Fewer than three LOIs by month 12, or many LOIs with no close.
requests.verify: Ask two investors about the history.

requests.request: Search-capital budget and actual spend split into searcher salary and deal costs.
requests.why: Median searcher salary $100K is 45% to 60% of search capital; spend mostly on salary with few LOIs is a red flag.
requests.pass: Spend in line with medians ($450K solo, $649K partnered) and producing LOIs.
requests.fail: Search capital spent mostly on salary with fewer than three LOIs by month 12.
requests.verify: Tie to bank statements of the search vehicle.

requests.request: Target CIM.
requests.why: Starting point for revenue, margin and customer story.
requests.pass: CIM received and claims tested in confirmatory.
requests.verify: Test each claim against tax returns.

requests.request: Purchase price and implied EBITDA and revenue multiples, with the share of recurring revenue.
requests.why: International median acquisition: $12M price, 5.7x EBITDA, 1.4x revenue, 26% margin.
requests.pass: Multiple at or near the about 5.7x median, or above it with recurring revenue to justify.
requests.fail: Multiple well above 5.7x without recurring revenue.

requests.request: LOI and draft purchase agreement key terms: price, structure, working capital, reps, indemnities, escrow.
requests.why: Lower-middle-market mechanics follow Chapter 5.
requests.pass: Terms consistent with Chapter 5 market norms.

requests.request: Sources and uses with total leverage including the seller note, and the equity cushion.
requests.why: Over-leverage on a small, cyclical business breaches covenants in a mild downturn.
requests.pass: Total leverage including seller note supportable in the 20% revenue-decline case.
requests.fail: Leverage only works in base case.

requests.request: SBA 7(a) or senior loan term sheet, including personal-guarantee requirements.
requests.why: SBA loans require personal guarantees (bible terms not primary-sourced; confirm current SBA SOP).
requests.pass: Terms confirmed against current SBA SOP; guarantee obligations understood.
requests.verify: Confirm with lender and current SBA SOP.

requests.request: Seller note terms: amount, subordination and standstill to the senior lender, and any tie to customer retention.
requests.why: Relationship revenue may leave with the seller.
requests.pass: Note subordinated with standstill; part tied to customer retention.
requests.fail: Unsubordinated note or no retention tie.

requests.request: Earn-out terms, including metrics and link to customer retention.
requests.why: Seller relationships drive revenue; earn-outs align transition.
requests.pass: Earn-out tied to retention metrics measurable from bank data.

requests.request: Seller transition and employment agreement: length, role, and compensation.
requests.why: Seller unwilling to stay is a red flag; seller typically stays 6 to 12 months (2007 practitioner figure).
requests.pass: Seller committed to a defined transition (6 to 12 months typical) with incentives.
requests.fail: Seller unwilling to stay for transition.

requests.request: Post-close board composition and the CEO-replacement right.
requests.why: A first-time CEO needs an experienced board with power to replace him or her; 69% of buyouts change CEO during the hold.
requests.pass: Board led by experienced lead investors with an operator who has run this kind of business; CEO-replacement right.
requests.fail: No CEO-replacement right or no operating experience on the board.

requests.request: Acquisition-round equity terms and pro forma cap table, including the step-up conversion of search capital.
requests.why: Investors' economics depend on step-up and searcher dilution.
requests.pass: Cap table reconciles to LPA step-up and searcher tranches.

requests.request: Three to five years of federal tax returns for the target.
requests.why: Small targets often have only tax-basis books; tax returns are the anchor for rebuilding EBITDA.
requests.pass: Returns match IRS transcripts and tie to QoE revenue within 2%.
requests.fail: Returns unavailable or materially below CIM revenue.
requests.verify: Obtain IRS transcripts with seller authorization.

requests.request: Internal monthly P&L and balance sheets for 36 months reconciled to tax returns.
requests.why: Tax-basis books need reconciling to management figures.
requests.pass: Monthly totals reconcile to returns.

requests.request: Customer list with revenue by customer for 3 years and concentration analysis.
requests.format: Ledger-based report tied to bank deposits.
requests.why: Customer concentration and churn after transition.
requests.pass: No customer above a level the FCCR stress survives losing; retention history stable.

requests.request: Map of customer relationships showing which are personal to the seller.
requests.why: Relationship revenue leaves with the seller.
requests.pass: Relationships transferable; seller introductions planned.
requests.fail: Key relationships personal to the seller with no transition plan.

requests.request: Owner add-back schedule with documentary support for each adjustment.
requests.format: Schedule with invoices and payroll records.
requests.why: Owner add-backs are the main source of overstatement in owner-run businesses.
requests.pass: Every add-back supported and non-recurring or truly personal.
requests.fail: Add-backs that are real operating costs.

requests.request: EBITDA rebuilt with the seller's labor replaced at a market salary.
requests.why: THE ONE CHECK: seller's unpaid labor overstates EBITDA.
requests.pass: Deal still meets FCCR and return targets on rebuilt EBITDA.

requests.request: Capex study: maintenance versus growth capex and deferred maintenance.
requests.why: Deferred capex is a hidden cost; capital-intensive targets with growth shortfalls failed.
requests.pass: Maintenance capex funded within FCCR stress.

requests.request: Capital-intensity assessment of the target relative to growth plan.
requests.why: Failures cluster in capital-intensive targets whose growth fell short (2007 podcast source).
requests.pass: Growth plan does not depend on large capex.

requests.request: Key-employee list with compensation and retention arrangements.
requests.why: Key employees leave with the seller.
requests.pass: Retention arrangements for each key employee.
requests.verify: Interview key employees pre-close where permitted.

requests.request: Fixed-charge coverage in a 20% revenue-decline case.
requests.why: Over-leverage breaches covenants in a mild downturn.
requests.pass: FCCR remains above the senior lender's covenant in the 20% decline case.

requests.request: Return model with exit multiple equal to entry multiple.
requests.why: About 80% of value in search-fund exits came from multiple expansion (6.3x to 15.6x).
requests.pass: Deal returns capital with a reasonable IRR at exit multiple equal to entry.
requests.fail: Deal works only with a re-rating.

requests.request: Value-creation plan split between EBITDA growth and multiple expansion, with margin assumptions.
requests.why: Margins fell from 25% to 19% in the Yale exit sample.
requests.pass: EBITDA growth drives the plan; margins not assumed to expand without evidence.

requests.request: 100-day plan.
requests.why: First-time CEO execution stalls.
requests.pass: Specific, owner-assigned actions for transition, customers and employees.

requests.request: CEO succession path and coaching plan for the first-time CEO.
requests.why: 69% of buyouts change CEO during the hold.
requests.pass: Named interim options and coach.

requests.request: For franchise targets: franchise agreement and FDD, including Item 17 and any no-poach or non-solicit clauses.
requests.format: Executed franchise agreement and current FDD.
requests.why: About 58% of major franchisors' 2016 agreements had no-poach clauses; AG and class actions followed.
requests.pass: No no-poach clause, or removed before close with no open exposure.

requests.request: Review of no-poach and wage-fixing provisions in multi-unit, staffing or franchise agreements, and any related claims.
requests.why: AG actions and class actions.
requests.pass: No such provisions or exposure.

requests.request: Non-compete enforceability analysis by state for seller and key employees.
requests.why: Unenforceable non-competes leave relationships unprotected.
requests.pass: Enforceable or alternative protections used.

requests.request: Diligence budget and scope by workstream, approved by investors.
requests.why: Adverse diligence findings killed 59% of failed deals; budget for diligence that kills deals.
requests.pass: Budget funds QoE, legal and customer calls.
requests.fail: Diligence cut to save cost ('too small').

requests.request: Quality of earnings report with proof of cash against tax returns and bank statements, and its engagement letter.
requests.format: QoE report and signed engagement letter; read the scope (a QoE carries no assurance).
requests.why: No QoE ('too small') is a red flag; owner-run P&Ls carry personal expenses.
requests.pass: QoE completed with proof of cash; scope covers revenue, add-backs and working capital.
requests.fail: No QoE, or scope excludes proof of cash.
requests.verify: Read engagement letter scope; call the provider.

requests.request: Customer calls before close with at least the top customers by revenue.
requests.why: Customer relationships personal to the seller; no customer calls allowed before close is a red flag.
requests.pass: Top customers confirm intent to continue post-transition.
requests.fail: Calls refused or customers signal departure.
requests.verify: Calls made by searcher and an investor.

requests.request: References from the searcher's prior managers and from investors in the search fund.
requests.why: Underwriting a first-time CEO.
requests.pass: Consistent positive references on execution and judgment.
requests.verify: Source at least one reference independently.

requests.request: Background check on the seller.
requests.why: Seller integrity drives reps and transition.
requests.pass: No undisclosed litigation or liens.

requests.request: Lender's counsel and our counsel review of loan documents, intercreditor and seller-note subordination.
requests.why: Leverage and guarantee terms.
requests.pass: Terms as agreed.

requests.request: Employment counsel review of non-compete, no-poach and transition agreements.
requests.why: No-poach exposure; unenforceable non-competes.
requests.pass: Agreements enforceable; no no-poach.

requests.request: Identification of experienced board members and, where used, a CEO coach.
requests.why: First-time CEO overwhelmed.
requests.pass: At least one board member has run this kind of business.

requests.request: Executed purchase agreement, seller note and subordination/standstill agreement.
requests.why: Seller note priority.
requests.pass: Executed as agreed.

requests.request: Executed seller transition and employment agreement.
requests.why: Seller leaves on day one.
requests.pass: Executed.

requests.request: Executed shareholders' agreement with board composition and CEO-replacement right.
requests.why: Governance.
requests.pass: Executed.

requests.request: Executed searcher equity and vesting documents.
requests.why: Full vesting at close.
requests.pass: Tranches as agreed.

requests.request: Executed senior loan documents and intercreditor.
requests.why: Leverage terms.
requests.pass: Executed as agreed.

requests.request: Signed key-employee retention agreements.
requests.why: Key-employee departures.
requests.pass: Signed for all key employees.

requests.request: Evidence that any no-poach clauses were unwound before close.
requests.why: AG action.
requests.pass: Unwound.

requests.request: Monthly financials and KPIs against the 100-day plan and budget.
requests.why: Execution stalls.
requests.pass: Delivered within 30 days; variances explained.

requests.request: Quarterly covenant and fixed-charge coverage compliance certificates.
requests.why: Covenant breach.
requests.pass: Compliant with cushion.

requests.request: Customer retention report after transition.
requests.why: Relationship revenue leaving.
requests.pass: Top-customer revenue retained.

requests.request: Annual reviewed or audited financial statements and tax returns.
requests.why: Reporting quality.
requests.pass: Delivered on time.

requests.request: Quarterly board minutes.
requests.why: Governance.
requests.pass: Board meets quarterly.

requests.request: Annual CEO assessment and succession review.
requests.why: CEO change mid-hold.
requests.pass: Completed annually.

requests.request: Seller-note and earn-out milestone tracking.
requests.why: Disputes.
requests.pass: Tracked.

kill_tests.test: No QoE with proof of cash against tax returns and bank statements ('too small').
Deal fails return or FCCR targets once seller labor is replaced at market salary.
Deal returns capital only with exit multiple above entry.
Fixed-charge coverage breaches the senior covenant in a 20% revenue-decline case.
No customer calls allowed before close where relationships are personal to the seller.

red_flags.flag: Purchase multiple well above the about 5.7x international median without recurring revenue.
Seller unwilling to stay for transition.
Searcher's equity vests fully at close.
Search capital spent mostly on salary with fewer than three LOIs by month 12.
Customer relationships personal to the seller; no customer calls allowed before close.
Model needs multiple expansion to return capital.
Capital-intensive target with a growth plan needing heavy capex.
No-poach or wage-fixing clause in franchise agreement.
Unsubordinated seller note or no standstill.

metrics.acceptable: About 21% (about a third of those total loss)

third_party_reports.report: Quality of earnings with proof of cash to tax returns and bank statements

third_party_reports.provider: Lender (SBA 7(a) or senior) and lender's counsel

third_party_reports.report: Background checks on searcher and seller

third_party_reports.provider: Experienced board members; CEO coach where used

hard_questions.question: What would you pay if the seller left on day one?
hard_questions.good_answer: A price based on EBITDA with seller labor replaced and relationship revenue haircut.

hard_questions.question: What does EBITDA look like with a market-rate replacement for the seller?
hard_questions.good_answer: A QoE-supported figure that still supports the price.

hard_questions.question: Who on the board has run this kind of business?
hard_questions.good_answer: A named operator with relevant experience.

hard_questions.question: Which three customers would you call first, and have you?
hard_questions.good_answer: Named customers already called, with notes.

hard_questions.question: What is the return at exit multiple equal to entry multiple?
hard_questions.good_answer: Positive return with capital returned from EBITDA growth and debt paydown.

hard_questions.question: What is fixed-charge coverage if revenue falls 20%?
How many LOIs have you signed, and why did the others die?
hard_questions.good_answer: A short, credible history, first LOI by about month six.

failure_cases.case: Owner add-backs that are real operating costs (generic)
failure_cases.what_happened: EBITDA overstated at entry (seller's unpaid labor, deferred capex).
failure_cases.check: Replace the seller's labor at market salary; capex study.

failure_cases.case: Relationship revenue that leaves with the seller (generic)
failure_cases.check: Customer calls before close; transition agreement with earn-out or seller note tied to retention.
Board with operating experience; 100-day plan; CEO coaching; succession plan.

failure_cases.case: Over-leverage on a small, cyclical business (generic)
failure_cases.what_happened: Covenant breach in a mild downturn.
failure_cases.check: Fixed-charge coverage in a 20% revenue-decline case.

failure_cases.what_happened: Exit at entry multiple leaves little return; margins fell in the sample.
failure_cases.check: Show return with exit multiple = entry multiple.
Capex study; maintenance vs growth capex split.

failure_cases.case: No-poach or wage-fixing clause in a franchise target (generic)
